column1: # Every compiled default/no-op/unsupported body candidate must match exactly one
# first-priority review rule. These rules classify implementation evidence; they
# do not add product exclusions or turn unfinished behavior into an exclusion.

column8: The inert packer/unpacker is a non-product compatibility boundary for the existing MessagePack exclusion; no product contract row targets it.
Reviewed .NET stream, iterator, filesystem, HTTP, and Java-compatibility defaults match their capability and mutability contracts.
The native runtime replacement exposes a stable false cancellation default and concrete cancellation paths override it.
Reviewed Truffle replacement hook defaults are intentionally nullable, false, or no-op and are overridden on behavior-bearing paths.
These inert compatibility hooks are reachable only behind the existing YAML exclusion and are not product API behavior.
Reviewed generic collection defaults implement the declared .NET collection contract.

The pinned upstream declaration and generated source were reviewed: nullable misses, false capability flags, immutable-operation failures, visitor hooks, lifecycle no-ops, and identity defaults are intentional semantics rather than stubs.
